title: feature-prio-hypothesis-scrub-elliot-2026-05-02
agenda: Quick context: why this scrub (timeline + exec ask)
Hypotheses review: 3 candidate features and expected user impact
Cost/latency tradeoff analysis per hypothesis (eng input)
Operational risk and rollout constraints (SRE & solutions)
Decision: pick 1 primary + 1 experiment for next sprint
Align on owners, measurement plan, and follow-ups
context_summary: Exec asked for a concrete plan to bend per-token cost for standard chat workloads while preserving 95th pct latency and quality. Product wants a prioritized feature to show immediate impact for Q3 roadmap review. We have three competing hypotheses: smarter batching + prefix cache tuning, model quantization variant + fallback, and routing by model variant with region-aware cost policies.
key_discussion_points: Hypothesis A (batch/cache): low engineering change, medium SLO risk; expect 8-15% cost improvement on steady-state traffic with KV cache warm paths
Hypothesis B (quantized variant): highest cost upside (20-40%) but requires model onboarding + evals; risk of small quality regressions and additional inference infra work for kernel paths
Hypothesis C (routing + market segmentation): operationally complex (policy engine + metrics), lower immediate upside but safer from quality perspective
Measurement: need clear sentinel prompts and holdout traffic to detect regressions (Marco to propose initial eval set)
Capacity: Dedicated pools could simplify rollout for B but requires reserved capacity commit—finance check needed
SLOs: 95th latency budget must be maintained. If A reduces token compute but increases tail latency due to batching delays, it's a net loss for real-time apps
decisions: Select Hypothesis A (batch/cache tuning) as primary immediate deliverable for 2-week spike
Run Hypothesis B as gated experiment in parallel: start quantization evals but do not route traffic until quality gates pass
Delay Hypothesis C until after initial A/B results and cost signal from A
Measurement baseline: use last 30 days chat traffic metrics; define cost-per-1000-requests and 95th latency targets
open_questions: How many production customers will be impacted during warm-cache transient? (Daniel to poll 3 top customers)
Do we have GPU memory headroom across regions to enable larger batch sizes without OOM? (Aisha to check infra telemetry)
What are the minimal quality tests for quantized variants that we trust? (Marco to propose and include regression thresholds)
If quantized model fails gating, what is the rollback SLA for customers on Dedicated? (SRE input needed)
action_items: Elliot: Draft one-paragraph exec summary and share with VP by 2026-05-06
Aisha: Run infra capacity check (GPU mem, scheduling headroom) for top 3 regions by 2026-05-05
Marco: Produce evaluation seed set (50 prompts + acceptance thresholds) for quantized variant by 2026-05-07
Sofia: Sketch measurement dashboard (cost / 95th latency / quality regression) and template for canary by 2026-05-08
Daniel: Identify 3 customers to invite for early feedback and any contracts that block routing changes by 2026-05-09
Priya (optional): Define rollback runbook and incident playbook for experiment B by 2026-05-10
notes: Scrap pad: think in terms of incremental wins. A is cheap and visible; B is strategic but heavy. We can stage A as 'platform defaults' and ship change notes. Watch out for tail latency — do not sacrifice 95th for median savings. Also consider short-lived burst windows where batching hurts UX.
follow_up_plan: After 2-week spike: present results in crossfunc review (15-min slot) with metrics snapshot. If A hits >10% cost savings and <1% quality delta, graduate to rollout plan. Keep B in eval pipeline and schedule a canary window (customer opt-in). Update roadmap doc and tag feature for Q3 deliverable.
